instructions: Add one confirmed row per concrete evidence item. Cite canonical source files, copy verifier excerpts verbatim, and judge source presence separately from recovery.

criteria.criterion: Use official npm Registry response at specified URL
criteria.description: Agent attempts to consult the official npm Registry JSON response from https://registry.npmjs.org/typescript/latest and uses it as the source for all requested fields. Full credit if the agent clearly indicates the URL is inaccessible (e.g., downtime/network/CAPTCHA/blocking) and therefore the registry response could not be retrieved. Partial credit if another source is used only after a clear attempt to use the specified URL (and the limitation is explained). No credit if values are provided without evidence or without attempting the specified URL.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot evidence analyses 1 & 2 show a raw JSON payload in an npm-registry-style viewer (“Pretty-print” checkbox) containing standard registry fields and registry.npmjs.org links (e.g., dist.tarball points to https://registry.npmjs.org/typescript/-/typescript-7.0.2.tgz). The address bar is not visible, so the exact endpoint cannot be visually confirmed, but the content strongly matches the official npm Registry response format for /typescript/latest.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Given the screenshots show an authentic-looking npm registry JSON payload for TypeScript with registry-hosted tarball URLs, it is reasonable to credit the agent with using the official registry response despite the URL bar not being shown. This addresses the baseline’s lack-of-evidence concern.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows a browser page with raw JSON content. Near the top-left there is a UI label “Pretty-print” with an unchecked box. In the JSON, fields like "dist": {"shasum":..., "tarball":"https://registry.npmjs.org/typescript/-/typescript-7.0.2.tgz", "fileCount":416, ...} are visible, and there are multiple "npmjs.org"/"registry.npmjs.org" URLs in the text (e.g., tarball and bugs/repository links). The specific address bar/URL “https://registry.npmjs.org/typescript/latest” is not visible in the screenshot.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The visible content is consistent with an official npm Registry JSON response for TypeScript (it includes the registry tarball URL under registry.npmjs.org and typical registry metadata fields). However, since the screenshot does not display the browser’s address bar or the exact URL, it cannot be visually confirmed that it was retrieved specifically from https://registry.npmjs.org/typescript/latest (though the content strongly suggests it).
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent claims use of the official npm Registry response at https://registry.npmjs.org/typescript/latest; the screenshot shows registry-style JSON but does not explicitly show the exact URL in an address bar.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows a raw JSON response in a browser-like viewer with a “Pretty-print” checkbox at top. In the visible JSON, there are TypeScript-related fields including `"name":"typescript"` and npm registry style keys like `"dist":{...}` and `"repository":{ "url":"git+https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript.git" ... }`. No URL bar is visible in the screenshot, so `https://registry.npmjs.org/typescript/latest` is not explicitly shown.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The content displayed is consistent with an npm Registry JSON payload for TypeScript (it includes standard registry fields and TypeScript metadata). While the specified URL is not visible, the screenshot supports that the agent used an official-registry-style JSON response as the data source.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent claims the source is `https://registry.npmjs.org/typescript/latest`, but the screenshot does not display the URL, only the JSON content. Otherwise, the visible content aligns with an npm registry response.

criteria.description: Agent does not download/install the package and stops after recording all six requested fields (name, version, license, engines.node requirement, dist.unpackedSize, dist.fileCount). Full credit if the agent either (a) provides exactly the requested fields when the registry response is accessible, or (b) if the registry response is inaccessible, clearly states it cannot retrieve the fields and stops without adding unrelated content or fabricated values. Partial credit if minor extra, non-misleading info is included but constraints are otherwise followed. No credit if the agent downloads/installs the package or fabricates values as if confirmed.

evidence_analyses.discrepancies: None apparent; the screenshot content supports the six extracted fields and does not show prohibited actions.
